parameter_status: All numerical presets are illustrative, not manufacturer-calibrated or measured site data.
motivation: User-supplied Michael Job article, Nvidia's 800-Volt Data Center Is Waiting on a Circuit Breaker, 2026-11-12. Used as a research question, not measurement data. No article text or photographs redistributed.

sources.supports: 54 V rack distribution, proposed 800 V delivery, MW-scale racks and retained rack DC/DC conversion.
sources.model_use: Topology context only. No hardcoded 5% saving, copper percentage or TCO benefit.

sources.supports: Migration through power racks, row power centers and facility DC power blocks.
sources.model_use: Scenario labels, not deployment predictions. Row preset retaining AC UPS is a study assumption.

sources.supports: Sections 2-3: isolation, grounding, mechanical protection, fuses, SSCBs and capacitor backfeed.
sources.model_use: Motivates separate isolation times and stored-energy accounting. This implementation does not reproduce the paper's transient network or its peak-current results.

sources.supports: Architecture, stored energy, reverse blocking and protection timing affect the studied fault cases; system-specific assessment is required.
sources.evidence_type: publisher summary of WP219 and document metadata; not an independent validation
sources.model_use: Research context. No incident-energy threshold, PPE classification or safety pass/fail is implemented.

sources.supports: Catalog identifies an Outline of Investigation; scope includes semiconductor switching and integral galvanic isolation for SSCB/SSHCB devices.
sources.evidence_type: official public catalog scope, not full certification requirements
sources.model_use: No claim that an outline prohibits certification or that any named device is certified.

unverified_or_excluded: Ulanqab capacity, topology, measured efficiency and protection arrangement are not independently established here; the 5 MW example is synthetic.
No certification deadline, country-wide deployment ban or approval prediction is inferred.
No battery-chemistry safety or commercial-readiness claim from social-media comments is used.
Removing a standalone AC UPS does not eliminate backup energy or rectification inside an SST.
A semiconductor switch alone does not establish protection coordination, galvanic isolation or certification.
